title: Get Zedu named correctly in AI assistant answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) by Fri 4 Dec
description:
More educators now ask AI assistants "what's the best tool to run a cohort?" instead of searching. Zedu has nothing set up for this: on 22 Oct 2026, zedu.chat/llms.txt, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml all return the app's HTML page instead of a real file (checked with curl), so AI crawlers get no clear map of the site. No other goal covers AI search.

Work under this goal:
- Baseline: ask 15 real buyer questions (from the keyword map or public forums) in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google, and record whether Zedu is named and whether what is said about it is accurate, with screenshots and the date.
- Publish a real llms.txt that lists Zedu's key pages with one honest line each (only facts the site states).
- Make the product and pricing pages easy for AI to quote: a clear one-line answer near the top of each page saying what it does and who it is for.
- Re-run the same 15 questions after the changes and compare.

Done when: zedu.chat/llms.txt returns a real text file, the before and after table for the 15 questions is delivered with sources, and any wrong statements about Zedu found in the answers are listed with the page fix for each. Nothing invented; every claim links to a source.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Fix the facts an AI would quote wrongly first, then re-measure the 15 questions
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The goal is to be NAMED CORRECTLY, and the baseline already shows Zedu is named in 0 of 30 completed answers (Google AI Overview 15, Perplexity 15, 22 Oct 2026) - with ChatGPT unmeasured. Before asking why AI omits Zedu, fix the facts it would get wrong if it did answer. Two defects are already verified and dated: (1) on https://zedu.chat/pricing the plan cards read Starter, Pro and Enterprise while the comparison table underneath is headed Starter, Growth, Enterprise, and the Pro card says 'Everything in Zedu Free' - three names for two plans on one page; (2) the site serves no llms.txt, robots.txt or sitemap.xml (all return the app HTML), so a crawler has no canonical spelling of any name or number to learn from.

Deliverables:
1) A canonical fact sheet - product names (Channels, Buzz), plan names, prices, what each plan includes, the one-line 'what Zedu is and who it is for' - each row with the live URL it comes from, and a flag wherever the site currently disagrees with itself.
2) Per disagreement, the exact page and the exact string to change, so the fix is one edit rather than a rewrite.
3) A 'what an AI should say about Zedu' block: 40-60 words, built only from the fact sheet, ready to drop into pages so any assistant quoting Zedu quotes the same sentence.
4) The re-measure step: once the fact sheet is approved and the naming fixed, re-run the same 15 buyer questions in Perplexity and Google AI Overview (ChatGPT needs a signed-in session - flagged, already escalated on the baseline task) and diff the answers against the fact sheet, so 'correctly' is measured rather than asserted.

Why it fits this goal and not the two accepted approaches: Irfat's workstream makes the site crawlable and KHALIF's writes pages for the queries competitors already win. This one removes the reason an assistant would get Zedu wrong even if it did answer - a site that names its own plans two different ways cannot be quoted accurately.
